BasisKind.description: What kind of authoring basis backs a pathway's causal edge.
BasisKind.title: BasisKind

BehaviorPart.description: A part naming a behavior: something that happened, or under ``role: condition``, had to.

absent.description: The behavior must NOT occur for the pathway to hold. The part still belongs to the composition; what is asserted is its absence.
absent.title: Absent

id.description: The behavior entry's kl- id, or `OWED` where the part names a requirement no entry fills yet.
id.title: Id

kind.description: Which side of the transcript the behavior sits on. Must match the target entry's `type`, and names the list the id is found in.
kind.title: Kind

owed.description: No entry fills this part yet. `id` is `OWED` and `owed_behavior` states what would fill it.
owed.title: Owed

owed_behavior.description: What an entry filling this part would have to assert, written so someone could author it. Required when `owed`.
owed_behavior.title: Owed Behavior

role.description: What this part does here. `condition` gates the claim; every other value composes it.

BehaviorPart.title: BehaviorPart

CasePassage.description:
A passage from a source about one person in it.

Cited where the source describes individual cases, such as a table of
participants' reported experiences, and the passage shows that person
reporting or displaying what the entry or edge asserts.

impact_class_in_source.description: The source's own name for the category the passage falls under.
impact_class_in_source.title: Impact Class In Source

licenses.description: What this passage establishes, in the citation's own words.
licenses.title: Licenses

limits.description: What the passage does not establish, such as a reported concern where the entry asserts a measured change.
limits.title: Limits

locator.description: Where in the source: section, table, figure, or page.
locator.title: Locator

participant.description: The source's label for the person the passage is about, such as P23.
participant.title: Participant

quote.description: The passage, verbatim from the source.
quote.title: Quote

quote_form.description: What kind of passage the quote is, such as a participant's own words or the authors' description of a case.
quote_form.title: Quote Form

source.description: The work cited: the `id` of a source entry.
source.title: Source

CasePassage.title: CasePassage

CitationDisposition.description: What a search of a source found for the entry, where it found no support.
CitationDisposition.title: CitationDisposition

Claim.description: One atomic, independently falsifiable assertion the entry makes.

grounding_eligible.description: False when no citation can support this claim, so its having none is not a gap in the evidence: for example, a boundary against another catalog entry, which is settled by the two definitions. Omitted when citations can attach.
grounding_eligible.title: Grounding Eligible

id.description: Local id, unique within the entry, e.g. 'c1'.
id.title: Id

kind.description: What kind of assertion this claim makes.

text.description: The claim in one sentence, stated so it could be false.
text.title: Text

Claim.title: Claim

ClaimEvidence.description:
External evidence, one row per claim-source pair.

Not a bibliographic reference: the same passage from the same paper appears
once per claim it licenses, with ``licenses`` stating what it establishes for
that claim specifically. Counting rows counts attachments, not works cited.

bridge.description: The stated inference from what the source shows to what the claim asserts. Required for adjacent and analogical fit.
bridge.title: Bridge

claim_id.description: The local claim id this row attaches to.
claim_id.title: Claim Id

contradicts.description: The quote cuts against the claim. Required true when contributes is counterexample.
contradicts.title: Contradicts

contributes.description: The evidence role this citation plays. Four of the ten values cannot license an occurrence claim.

fit.description: Domain distance between the source and the claim. Independent of `contributes`, which is the role the quote plays.

licenses.description: What this quote establishes FOR THIS CLAIM, in the citation's own words. Must be at least as strong as the claim it supports.
licenses.title: Licenses

locator.description: Where in the source: section, table, figure, or page. A directory path is not a locator.
locator.title: Locator

quote.description: Verbatim from the source, machine-verified after normalization. A paraphrase fails.
quote.title: Quote

source.description: The work cited: the `id` of a source entry.
source.title: Source

ClaimEvidence.title: ClaimEvidence

ClaimKind.description: What kind of assertion a claim makes.
ClaimKind.title: ClaimKind

CompositionRow.description: One constituent of a composite entry.

role.description: What the constituent contributes to the composite.
role.title: Role

CompositionRow.title: CompositionRow

CompositionType.description:
How a pathway's OBSERVATIONS compose.

One field per semantic: the impact structure derives from ``impacts[]``,
and conditionality is carried by the parts whose role is condition-like.

Scopes to ``observations()``, not to every part: a condition-role part is
not part of the composition this names.

``cascade`` is the exception: it describes an ordering between impact edges,
because no other field holds the order of one impact after another.

Each value's description makes a claim about how many observations the
pathway has. Read it as what the value asserts, not as a rule enforced
here.
CompositionType.title: CompositionType

Contested.description: An open question about whether the entry should exist as stated.

summary.description: The question, and what each answer would mean for the entry. States the dispute; does not recount how it arose.
summary.title: Summary

Contested.title: Contested

ContextPart.description: A part naming a context value: a fact the test case must hold for the pathway to apply.

absent.description: The negation: the test case records a value on the dimension and it is not this one. An unrecorded dimension satisfies neither this part nor its negation.
absent.title: Absent

kind.description: Fixed: the part names a context value.
kind.title: Kind

role.description: Always `condition`: a context value gates the claim and never composes it.
role.title: Role

ContextPart.title: ContextPart

Contributes.description:
The evidence role a citation plays.

Four values are not support. Non-licensing means cannot license an
OCCURRENCE claim, not licenses nothing: ``frame`` still reaches ``theorized``
and ``practice_analog`` reaches ``extrapolated_from_clinical``.
Contributes.title: Contributes

DistinguishFrom.description: A boundary statement against a neighbouring entry.

boundary.description: What separates this entry from that neighbour. Resolves a judge's disagreement about which of two adjacent entries applies.
boundary.title: Boundary

DistinguishFrom.title: DistinguishFrom

EntrySource.description:
A source cited against the entry as a whole rather than against one claim.

Kept beside ``claim_evidence``, whose rows each attach to a claim. Here
``cited_for`` says in prose what the passage is cited for.

actually_licenses.description: What the passage supports on a strict reading, where that is narrower than `licenses` or than the role in `contributes` suggests.
actually_licenses.title: Actually Licenses

cited_for.description: What the passage is cited for, in prose.
cited_for.title: Cited For

contributes.description: The evidence role this citation plays.

disposition.description: Set when the source was read for this entry and found to support nothing it asserts, or to cut against it.

evidence.description: Individual cases in the source that the citation rests on.
evidence.title: Evidence

licenses.description: What this passage establishes, in the citation's own words.
licenses.title: Licenses

limits.description: What the passage does not establish.
limits.title: Limits

locator.description: Where in the source: section, table, figure, or page.
locator.title: Locator

note.description: A fact about the passage a reader needs to weigh it.
note.title: Note

quote.description: The passage, verbatim from the source.
quote.title: Quote

source.description: The work cited: the `id` of a source entry.
source.title: Source

whose_conduct_in_passage.description: Whose conduct the passage shows. A passage showing only the AI's conduct says nothing observed about the person.

EntrySource.title: EntrySource

Fit.description:
Domain distance between source and claim.

Independent of ``contributes``, which is the role the quote plays; the two
axes must not be forced to agree. A citation that licenses nothing is
removed or its claim narrowed, so there is no value for that state.
Fit.title: Fit

Horizon.description: How soon the impact follows the behavior.
Horizon.title: Horizon

Layer.description: What kind of thing an entry asserts.
Layer.title: Layer

LevelOfAnalysis.description:
Whose outcome the edge is about.

A population-level finding does not license a within-person claim.
LevelOfAnalysis.title: LevelOfAnalysis

Lifecycle.description: Where the entry sits between authored and retired.

since.description: ISO date the entry entered this status.
since.title: Since

superseded_by.description: The entries that replace this one, by id. Only a deprecated entry names successors; one split in two names both. Empty when the entry was retired with nothing in its place.
superseded_by.title: Superseded By

Lifecycle.title: Lifecycle

Measurement.description: What it would take to measure the entry's construct in a transcript.

what_would_be_needed.description: The instrument or label that would measure the construct, and what existing instruments lack. Written where no surveyed instrument measures it.
what_would_be_needed.title: What Would Be Needed

Measurement.title: Measurement

PartRole.description:
What a part does in the pathway, and which view it falls into.

``role`` decides both derived views. A part whose role is ``condition`` is
returned by ``preconditions()``, the identity gate, where changing a member
makes it a different pathway. Every other value is returned by
``observations()``: what happened, and what ``composition_type`` describes.

A wrong role yields a wrong derived gate, so the role is the first thing
to check when a pathway's gate looks wrong.

A role belongs to the part, not to the behavior it names: the same
behavior legitimately originates one pathway and sustains another, and
normalizing a behavior to one role would change what those pathways
assert.
PartRole.title: PartRole

PassageConduct.description: Whose conduct a cited passage shows.
PassageConduct.title: PassageConduct

PathwayBody.description:
A route from what happened to an outcome, and the terms it holds under.

Composed of one authored list. ``composition_parts`` holds every term the
pathway is built from, and each part's ``role`` sorts it into one of two
derived views: ``preconditions()`` for the parts that gate the claim,
``observations()`` for the parts that compose it.

The preconditions are part of the pathway's identity. Two pathways with the
same observations and different preconditions are two entries. A condition
that changes how strongly a pathway holds is expressed that way too, as a
separate pathway, and there is no field for it.

composition_instruction.description: Composition that `composition_type` and the parts' roles cannot carry, in the entry's own terms. Read by the judge. Must say something the structure does not already say: never restates the type, a role, or a part's own criteria.
composition_instruction.title: Composition Instruction

composition_parts.description: The one authored list: everything the pathway is composed of or gated by. `observations()` and `preconditions()` are views over it, keyed on each part's `role`; neither is stored.
composition_parts.title: Composition Parts

composition_type.description: How the OBSERVATIONS compose. Scopes to `observations()`, not to every part: a condition-role part is not part of the composition this names.

counterpart_owed.description: A counterpart this pathway implies that nobody has authored: what a well-handled version of this situation would look like, where no entry states it.
counterpart_owed.title: Counterpart Owed

downstream.description: What this pathway's impact in turn feeds.
downstream.title: Downstream

experience_cluster_candidate.description: Flags the pathway as a candidate member of an experience cluster not yet composed.
experience_cluster_candidate.title: Experience Cluster Candidate

impacts.description: The impacts this pathway leads to.
impacts.title: Impacts

mechanism_hypothesis.description: A proposed mechanism not yet promoted to a mechanism entry.
mechanism_hypothesis.title: Mechanism Hypothesis

mechanisms.description: mechanism entries asserted to drive this pathway.
mechanisms.title: Mechanisms

mediators.description: What sits between the behavior and the outcome.
mediators.title: Mediators

standing_minimum_question.description: An open question about what this pathway's standing should be floored at.
standing_minimum_question.title: Standing Minimum Question

temporal.description: Timing structure beyond the impact horizon.
temporal.title: Temporal

treatment_competition_concern.description: Where the pathway may compete with a treatment the person is already receiving.
treatment_competition_concern.title: Treatment Competition Concern

PathwayBody.title: PathwayBody

basis_kind.description: How this causal edge was arrived at. Most edges are specification-derived rather than measured.

evidence.description: Passages from sources that bear on this edge.
evidence.title: Evidence

impact.description: The impact entry this pathway leads to.
impact.title: Impact

level_of_analysis.description: Whether the claim is about this person or a rate.

onset_mode.description: Whether the impact is new, worsened, foregone, or held in place.

sign.description: Whether the edge runs toward or away from harm. A protective pathway is not a failure to detect.

Standing.description:
Evidential standing.

The first six form an ordered evidence scale. The last four sit outside it:
every rung of the scale names a way of observing a person, and these do not.
Standing.title: Standing

StandingBlock.description:
The entry's evidential-strength verdict.

A judgment of what the cited sources actually observed, made by reading them
rather than by counting how citations are filed, and stated in ``basis``.
Entry standing is the minimum over grounding-eligible claims: an entry
asserts the conjunction of its claims, so it is only as observed as its
least observed part.
StandingBlock.title: StandingBlock

aliases.description: Other handles this entry is known by: readable names a consumer may show in place of the kl- id.
aliases.title: Aliases

body.description: A route from behaviors to an impact.

claim_evidence.description: External evidence, one row per claim-source pair.
claim_evidence.title: Claim Evidence

claims.description: The entry decomposed into atomic, independently falsifiable assertions. Grounding attaches here rather than to the entry.
claims.title: Claims

composed_of.description: Constituent entries, where the entry is a composite of others.
composed_of.title: Composed Of

contested.description: An open question about whether the entry should exist as stated.

context.description: References to standing context notes, which are statements about the territory that bear on many entries and license none of them.
context.title: Context

definition.description: The full prose definition: what must be true for this entry to apply. What a generator paraphrases into a persona instruction or system-knowledge fact.
definition.title: Definition

display_id.description: Human-facing handle, e.g. `Pathway-5`, for a report to show. Changes when an entry is re-familied, so a consumer looks entries up by `id`.
display_id.title: Display Id

distinguish_from.description: Boundary statements against neighbouring entries: what separates this from the thing it is most often confused with.
distinguish_from.title: Distinguish From

id.description: Stable identifier, `kl-` followed by six digits.
id.title: Id

label.description: Short human name for the entry.
label.title: Label

layer.description: What kind of thing the entry asserts.

lifecycle.description: Whether the entry is draft, active, or retired.

measurement.description: What it would take to measure the entry's construct, where no surveyed instrument does.

sources.description: Evidence cited against the whole entry rather than against a claim, kept alongside `claim_evidence`.
sources.title: Sources

standing.description: The entry's evidential-strength verdict, a judgment of what its cited sources observed, with the reasoning in `basis`.
